title_en: Advertising Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is enacted for the purposes of regulating advertising activities, protecting the lawful rights and interests of consumers, promoting the healthy development of the advertising industry, and maintaining the socio-economic order.

Article 2 This Law shall apply to commercial advertising activities within the territory of the People's Republic of China where a commodity operator or service provider directly or indirectly introduces the commodities or services it sells or provides through any medium or form.
For the purposes of this Law, an advertiser means any natural person, legal person, or other organization that designs, produces, and publishes advertisements by itself or by entrusting others for the purpose of selling commodities or providing services.
For the purposes of this Law, an advertising agent means any natural person, legal person, or other organization that provides advertising design, production, and agency services upon commission.
For the purposes of this Law, an advertising publisher means any natural person, legal person, or other organization that publishes advertisements for an advertiser or an advertising agent commissioned by an advertiser.
For the purposes of this Law, an advertising endorser means any natural person, legal person, or other organization other than the advertiser that recommends or certifies commodities or services in advertisements in its own name or image.

Article 3 Advertisements shall be true, lawful, and express the content in a healthy form, and shall comply with the requirements of the construction of socialist spiritual civilization and the promotion of the excellent traditional culture of the Chinese nation.

Article 4 Advertisements shall not contain false or misleading content, and shall not deceive or mislead consumers.
An advertiser shall be responsible for the truthfulness of the content of its advertisements.
Article 5 Advertisers, advertising agents, and advertising publishers engaging in advertising activities shall comply with laws and regulations, act in good faith, and compete fairly.

Article 6 The market supervision and administration department of the State Council shall be in charge of the supervision and administration of advertising nationwide, and the relevant departments of the State Council shall be responsible for the relevant advertising management work within their respective functions and duties.
The market supervision and administration departments of local people's governments at or above the county level shall be in charge of the supervision and administration of advertising within their respective administrative regions, and the relevant departments of local people's governments at or above the county level shall be responsible for the relevant advertising management work within their respective functions and duties.

Article 7 Advertising industry organizations shall, in accordance with laws, regulations, and their articles of association, formulate industry norms, strengthen self-discipline, promote industry development, guide their members to engage in advertising activities according to law, and promote the construction of integrity in the advertising industry.

Article 8 Where an advertisement expresses information on the performance, function, origin, use, quality, composition, price, producer, term of validity, promise, etc. of a commodity, or on the content, provider, form, quality, price, promise, etc. of a service, such information shall be accurate, clear, and explicit.
Where an advertisement indicates that commodities or services being promoted come with complimentary gifts, the variety, specification, quantity, term, and method of the complimentary gifts shall be clearly indicated.
Where laws or administrative regulations require that certain content shall be clearly indicated in an advertisement, such content shall be indicated prominently and clearly.
Article 10 Advertisements shall not harm the physical and mental health of minors or disabled persons.

Article 11 Where the matters involved in the content of an advertisement require an administrative license, the content shall be consistent with the licensed content.
Where an advertisement uses data, statistical information, survey results, abstracts, quotations, or other cited content, such content shall be true and accurate, and the source shall be indicated. Where the cited content has a scope of application or term of validity, such information shall be clearly indicated.

Article 12 Where a patent product or patent method is involved in an advertisement, the patent number and patent type shall be indicated.
Where a patent right has not been obtained, it shall not be falsely claimed in an advertisement that a patent right has been obtained.
The use of patent applications that have not been granted patent rights and patents that have been terminated, revoked, or invalidated for advertising purposes is prohibited.
Article 13 Advertisements shall not disparage the commodities or services of other producers or business operators.

Article 14 Advertisements shall be identifiable and enable consumers to discern them as advertisements.
Mass media shall not publish advertisements in the disguised form of news reports. Advertisements published through mass media shall be prominently marked with "advertisement" to distinguish them from other non-advertising information, and shall not cause consumer confusion.
Radio stations and television stations publishing advertisements shall comply with the provisions of the relevant departments of the State Council regarding duration and method, and shall provide obvious prompts regarding the advertising duration.

Article 15 Special drugs such as narcotic drugs, psychotropic drugs, toxic drugs for medical use, and radioactive drugs, as well as pharmaceutical precursor chemicals, and drugs, medical devices, and treatment methods for drug addiction treatment, shall not be advertised.
Prescription drugs other than those specified in the preceding paragraph may only be advertised in medical and pharmaceutical professional journals jointly designated by the health administrative department of the State Council and the drug regulatory department of the State Council.

Article 17 Except for advertisements for medical treatment, drugs, and medical devices, any other advertisement is prohibited from involving disease treatment functions, and shall not use medical terminology or wording likely to confuse the commodities being promoted with drugs or medical devices.

Article 19 Radio stations, television stations, press, audio and video publishing units, and Internet information service providers shall not publish advertisements for medical treatment, drugs, medical devices, or health foods in a disguised form, such as by introducing health or wellness knowledge.
Article 20 The publication of advertisements for infant dairy products, beverages, and other foods that claim to fully or partially replace breast milk in mass media or public places is prohibited.

Article 22: It shall be prohibited to publish tobacco advertisements in mass media, or in public places, public transport vehicles, or outdoors. It shall be prohibited to send any form of tobacco advertisements to minors.
It shall be prohibited to use advertisements for other goods or services, or public interest advertisements, to promote the name, trademark, packaging, decoration and similar content of tobacco products.
In notices of relocation, name change, recruitment, etc. published by tobacco product producers or sellers, the name, trademark, packaging, decoration and similar content of tobacco products shall not be included.

Article 29: Radio stations, television stations, and newspaper publishing units that engage in advertising publishing business shall establish a specialized institution for advertising business, equip it with necessary personnel, and have premises and equipment suitable for publishing advertisements.
Article 30: Advertisers, advertising operators, and advertising publishers shall enter into written contracts according to law in advertising activities.
Article 31: Advertisers, advertising operators, and advertising publishers shall not engage in any form of unfair competition in advertising activities.

Article 32: Where an advertiser commissions the design, production, or publication of an advertisement, it shall commission an advertising operator or advertising publisher that possesses lawful business qualifications.

Article 33: Where an advertiser or advertising operator uses the name or image of another person in an advertisement, it shall obtain the prior written consent of that person; where it uses the name or image of a person with no capacity for civil conduct or with limited capacity for civil conduct, it shall obtain the prior written consent of that person's guardian.

Article 34: Advertising operators and advertising publishers shall establish and improve systems for registration, review, and file management of advertising business acceptance in accordance with relevant State regulations.
Advertising operators and advertising publishers shall inspect relevant documentary evidence and verify advertising content in accordance with laws and administrative regulations. For advertisements with inconsistent content or incomplete documentary evidence, advertising operators shall not provide design, production, or agency services, and advertising publishers shall not publish them.
Article 35: Advertising operators and advertising publishers shall publish their fee standards and fee collection methods.
Article 36: Data such as coverage, viewership, click-through rate, and circulation provided by advertising publishers to advertisers and advertising operators shall be truthful.

Article 37: No unit or individual may design, produce, act as an agent for, or publish advertisements for products or services that are prohibited from being produced or sold, or for goods or services that are prohibited from being advertised, under laws and administrative regulations.

Article 38: An advertising endorser who makes recommendations or endorsements for goods or services in an advertisement shall do so based on facts, conform to the provisions of this Law and relevant laws and administrative regulations, and shall not make recommendations or endorsements for goods it has not used or services it has not received.
Minors under the age of ten shall not be used as advertising endorsers.
Where a natural person, legal person, or other organization has been subject to an administrative penalty for making recommendations or endorsements in a false advertisement within the three years prior, such person or organization shall not be used as an advertising endorser.

Article 39: Advertising activities shall not be conducted in primary and secondary schools or kindergartens. The use of textbooks, supplementary teaching materials, exercise books, stationery, teaching aids, school uniforms, school buses, etc. of primary and secondary school students and preschool children for publishing or disguising advertisements shall be prohibited, except for public interest advertisements.

Article 40: No advertisements for medical treatment, pharmaceuticals, health foods, medical devices, cosmetics, alcoholic beverages, beauty products, or online game advertisements that are detrimental to the physical and mental health of minors shall be published in mass media targeting minors.
Advertisements for goods or services targeting minors under the age of fourteen shall not contain the following:
(1) Inducing them to ask their parents to purchase the advertised goods or services;
(2) Content that may lead them to imitate unsafe behaviors.

Article 41 The local people's government at or above the county level shall organize the relevant departments to strengthen the supervision and administration of outdoor advertisements published by using outdoor places, spaces, facilities, etc., and shall formulate planning and safety requirements for the setting up of outdoor advertisements.
The administrative measures for outdoor advertisements shall be prescribed by local regulations and local government rules.

Article 43 No unit or individual may send advertisements to a party's residence, means of transportation, etc., without the consent or request of the party, nor may they send advertisements to the party by electronic information.
Where advertisements are sent by electronic information, the true identity and contact information of the sender shall be clearly indicated, and the receiver shall be provided with a method to refuse further receipt.

Article 44 The provisions of this Law shall apply to advertising activities conducted through the Internet.
Where advertisements are published or sent through the Internet, the normal use of the network by users shall not be affected. Advertisements published in the form of pop-ups or otherwise on Internet pages shall clearly indicate a close mark to ensure one-click closure.

Article 45 The administrator of a public place, or a telecommunications business operator or Internet information service provider that knows or should know that illegal advertisements are sent or published through its place or information transmission or publication platform, shall stop such acts.

Article 46 Advertisements for medical treatments, pharmaceuticals, medical devices, pesticides, veterinary drugs, and health foods, as well as other advertisements that shall be subject to examination according to laws and administrative regulations, shall have their content examined by the relevant department (hereinafter referred to as the advertisement examination authority) before publication; without examination, they shall not be published.

Article 47 An advertiser applying for advertisement examination shall submit relevant supporting documents to the advertisement examination authority in accordance with laws and administrative regulations.
The advertisement examination authority shall make an examination decision in accordance with laws and administrative regulations, and shall send a copy of the examination approval document to the market supervision and administration department at the same level. The advertisement examination authority shall promptly announce approved advertisements to the public.
Article 48 No unit or individual may forge, alter, or transfer the advertisement examination approval document.

Article 50 The market supervision and administration department of the State Council, together with the relevant departments of the State Council, shall formulate the code of conduct for the publication of advertisements in mass media.

Article 51 Where the market supervision and administration department exercises its powers in accordance with the provisions of this Law, the party shall assist and cooperate and shall not refuse or obstruct.

Article 52 The market supervision and administration department, the relevant departments, and their staff members shall have the obligation to keep confidential the trade secrets learned in the activities of advertising supervision and administration.

Article 53 Any unit or individual shall have the right to lodge a complaint or report to the market supervision and administration department or the relevant department any act that violates this Law. The market supervision and administration department and the relevant department shall make public the telephone number, mailbox, or email address for receiving complaints and reports. The department that receives a complaint or report shall, within seven working days from the date of receipt, handle the matter and inform the complainant or informant.
Where the market supervision and administration department or the relevant department fails to perform its duties according to law, any unit or individual shall have the right to report to its superior authority or the supervisory authority. The authority that receives the report shall handle it according to law and promptly inform the informant of the handling result.
The relevant department shall keep confidential the information of the complainant and the informant.

Article 54 Consumer associations and other consumer organizations shall, according to law, exercise social supervision over acts that violate the provisions of this Law, such as publishing false advertisements infringing upon the legitimate rights and interests of consumers, and other acts that harm the public interest.

Article 55 Where a false advertisement is published in violation of the provisions of this Law, the market supervision and administration department shall order the cessation of publication of the advertisement, order the advertiser to eliminate the effects within the corresponding scope, and impose a fine of not less than three times but not more than five times the advertising expenses; if the advertising expenses cannot be calculated or are obviously low, a fine of not less than 200,000 yuan but not more than 1,000,000 yuan shall be imposed. If there have been three or more illegal acts within two years or there are other serious circumstances, a fine of not less than five times but not more than ten times the advertising expenses shall be imposed; if the advertising expenses cannot be calculated or are obviously low, a fine of not less than 1,000,000 yuan but not more than 2,000,000 yuan shall be imposed, and the business license may be revoked, and the advertisement examination authority shall revoke the advertisement examination approval document and shall not accept its application for advertisement examination within one year.
Where a medical institution commits the illegal act as provided in the preceding paragraph and the circumstances are serious, in addition to the punishment imposed by the market supervision and administration department in accordance with this Law, the health administrative department may revoke the diagnosis and treatment subjects or the practice license of the medical institution.
Where an advertisement operator or advertisement publisher, knowing or should know that an advertisement is false, still designs, produces, acts as an agent, or publishes it, the market supervision and administration department shall confiscate the advertising expenses and impose a fine of not less than three times but not more than five times the advertising expenses; if the advertising expenses cannot be calculated or are obviously low, a fine of not less than 200,000 yuan but not more than 1,000,000 yuan shall be imposed; if there have been three or more illegal acts within two years or there are other serious circumstances, a fine of not less than five times but not more than ten times the advertising expenses shall be imposed; if the advertising expenses cannot be calculated or are obviously low, a fine of not less than 1,000,000 yuan but not more than 2,000,000 yuan shall be imposed, and the relevant department may suspend the advertisement publication business or revoke the business license.
Where an advertiser, advertisement operator, or advertisement publisher commits the acts provided in the first and third paragraphs of this Article, which constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 56 Where a false advertisement is published in violation of the provisions of this Law, deceiving or misleading consumers, thereby causing damage to the legitimate rights and interests of consumers who purchase goods or receive services, the advertiser shall bear civil liability according to law. If the advertisement operator or advertisement publisher cannot provide the true name, address, and effective contact information of the advertiser, the consumer may demand that the advertisement operator or advertisement publisher make compensation first.
Where a false advertisement for goods or services related to the life and health of consumers causes damage to consumers, the advertisement operator, advertisement publisher, and advertising spokesperson shall bear joint and several liability with the advertiser.
Where a false advertisement for goods or services other than those provided in the preceding paragraph causes damage to consumers, the advertisement operator, advertisement publisher, and advertising spokesperson who, knowing or should know that the advertisement is false, still design, produce, act as an agent, publish, or make recommendations or certifications, shall bear joint and several liability with the advertiser.

Article 60 Where an advertisement operator or advertisement publisher, in violation of Article 34 of this Law, fails to establish or improve an advertising business management system in accordance with the relevant provisions of the state, or fails to check the content of advertisements, the market supervision and administration department shall order rectification and may impose a fine of not more than 50,000 yuan.
Where an advertisement operator or advertisement publisher, in violation of Article 35 of this Law, fails to publicize its charging standards and methods, the price authority shall order rectification and may impose a fine of not more than 50,000 yuan.

Article 62 Any person who sends advertisements in violation of the provisions of Article 43 of this Law shall be ordered by the relevant department to cease the illegal act, and a fine of not less than 5,000 yuan but not more than 30,000 yuan shall be imposed on the advertiser.
Any person who, in violation of the provisions of Article 44, paragraph 2 of this Law, uses the internet to publish advertisements without conspicuously marking the close symbol and ensuring one-click closure, shall be ordered by the market supervision and administration department to make corrections, and a fine of not less than 5,000 yuan but not more than 30,000 yuan shall be imposed on the advertiser.

Article 63 Where a manager of a public place, a telecommunications business operator, or an internet information service provider, in violation of the provisions of Article 45 of this Law, knowing or should have known that an advertising activity is illegal, fails to stop it, the market supervision and administration department shall confiscate the illegal gains. If the illegal gains are 50,000 yuan or more, a fine of not less than one time but not more than three times the illegal gains shall also be imposed; if the illegal gains are less than 50,000 yuan, a fine of not less than 10,000 yuan but not more than 50,000 yuan shall also be imposed. If the circumstances are serious, the relevant department shall suspend the relevant business according to law.

Article 64 Where a person, in violation of the provisions of this Law, conceals the true situation or provides false materials to apply for an advertisement review, the advertisement review authority shall not accept or approve the application, issue a warning, and shall not accept any advertisement review application from the applicant within one year. Where the advertisement review approval is obtained by fraud, bribery, or other illegitimate means, the advertisement review authority shall revoke it, impose a fine of not less than 100,000 yuan but not more than 200,000 yuan, and shall not accept any advertisement review application from the applicant within three years.

Article 65 Where a person, in violation of the provisions of this Law, forges, alters, or transfers an advertisement review approval document, the market supervision and administration department shall confiscate the illegal gains and impose a fine of not less than 10,000 yuan but not more than 100,000 yuan.

Article 66 Where there is an illegal act as provided for in this Law, the market supervision and administration department shall record it in the credit file and publish it in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws and administrative regulations.

Article 67 Where a radio station, television station, newspaper, audio-visual publishing unit publishes illegal advertisements, or publishes advertisements in disguise in the form of news reports, or publishes advertisements for medical treatments, pharmaceuticals, medical devices, or health foods in disguise in the form of introducing health or wellness knowledge, and the market supervision and administration department imposes a penalty in accordance with this Law, it shall notify the competent departments of press and publication, radio and television, and other relevant departments. The competent departments of press and publication, radio and television, and other relevant departments shall, according to law, impose sanctions on the persons in charge directly responsible and the other persons directly responsible; if the circumstances are serious, they may also suspend the advertisement publishing business of the media.
If the competent departments of press and publication, radio and television, and other relevant departments fail to handle the matter against the radio station, television station, newspaper, audio-visual publishing unit in accordance with the preceding paragraph, sanctions shall be imposed according to law on the persons in charge directly responsible and the other persons directly responsible.

Article 69 Where a company or enterprise has its business license revoked for publishing false advertisements or for other illegal acts provided for in this Law, the legal representative of such company or enterprise who bears personal responsibility for the illegal act shall not serve as a director, supervisor, or senior officer of a company or enterprise within three years from the date of revocation of the business license.

Article 70 Any person who, in violation of the provisions of this Law, refuses or obstructs supervision and inspection by the market supervision and administration department, or commits other acts constituting a violation of public security administration, shall be given a public security administration penalty according to law; if the act constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 71 Where an advertisement review authority makes a decision to review and approve illegal advertisement content, the persons in charge directly responsible and the other persons directly responsible shall be given sanctions according to law by the appointment and removal authority or the supervisory authority; if the act constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 72 Where the market supervision and administration department fails to investigate and punish illegal advertising acts discovered during the performance of its advertising monitoring duties or illegal advertising acts reported through complaints or tip-offs according to law, the persons in charge directly responsible and the other persons directly responsible shall be given sanctions according to law.
Where a staff member of the market supervision and administration department or a relevant department responsible for advertising management related work neglects their duty, abuses their power, or engages in malpractices for personal gain, sanctions shall be given according to law.
Where an act mentioned in the preceding two paragraphs constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 73 The state encourages and supports the carrying out of public interest advertising campaigns to disseminate socialist core values and promote civilized customs.
The mass media has the obligation to publish public interest advertisements. Radio stations, television stations, and newspaper publishing units shall publish public interest advertisements in accordance with the prescribed layout, time slots, and duration. The administrative measures for public interest advertisements shall be formulated by the market supervision and administration department of the State Council in conjunction with the relevant departments.
Article 74 This Law shall come into force as of September 1, 2015.
